dedupe_keys.name: sndlib survivable fixed telecommunication network design library

description: SNDlib is a library of realistic telecommunication network instances for research on the design and operation of survivable fixed networks. Each of its 26 networks consists of nodes, edges with capacity and cost models, and a set of communication demands; examples include abilene (12 nodes, 15 links, 132 demands), geant (22, 36, 462), germany50 (50, 88, 662), nobel-eu, polska, janos-us and brain (161 nodes, 332 links, 14,311 demands). Several networks also have dynamic traffic matrices derived from measurements in real networks and mapped onto the topologies. SNDlib was announced at the DRCN 2005 conference by Michał Pióro (Warsaw University of Technology) and Roland Wessäly (atesio and Zuse Institute Berlin); a second version in 2011 added topologies and dynamic matrices; the third version keeps the topologies and demand matrices but drops the former problem descriptions and solutions, and moved in 2023 to Poznan University of Technology, where Filip Idzikowski maintains it with Christian Raack (atesio). Data are free to download as compressed archives (tgz or zip) in a native ASCII format or XML, with a GML variant documented, plus a Java library whose download asks users to accept the ZIB Academic License; users are asked to cite the two SNDlib references. Coverage is mostly European and North American backbones, with a few from other regions. Caveats: networks are research abstractions of real backbones at various dates, without geographic accuracy or equipment detail, and traffic matrices are static or historical. Simulation uses: benchmark topologies and demands for network flow, capacity planning, optimisation and survivability or cascading-failure studies of backbone networks. Related records: the Internet Topology Zoo and CAIDA topology datasets.
